subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: MWCC GC 1.2.5, cflags_demo game code (-inline auto). `#pragma auto_inline off` bracketing a CALLEE'S OWN DEFINITION forces every call site in the TU to emit a real `bl` WITHOUT changing the callee's own emitted bytes, and WITHOUT disturbing explicitly-`inline` helpers that inline into those same call sites. This DIRECTLY REFUTES the operative consequence of claim.law.dont-inline-pragma-is-function-granular-and-unoverridable.20260831.v1, which concluded that 'within a single function, forcing one callee to stay a real call and letting other helpers inline are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE' and that such a function 'cannot be closed by pragma placement at all'. That conclusion generalised from ONE pragma family (dont_inline / always_inline) to all of them; auto_inline is a different control and delivers exactly the combination the earlier law declared impossible. THE MECHANISM, and why the distinction is real: with `-inline auto`, MWCC has TWO inline populations. Functions carrying the `inline` keyword are EXPLICIT candidates; functions without it (an ordinary `void f(void){...}` defined earlier in the TU) are AUTOMATIC candidates. `auto_inline off` suppresses only the automatic population. In psfx.c LoadPlyrData the swap helpers sSwapU16/sSwapU32/sSwapF32 are `static inline` (explicit) and kept inlining across all 70 sites, while PlayerSfxInitData (no `inline` keyword, defined at psfx.c:1070 well before its two call sites) stopped being inlined and became `bl PlayerSfxInitData` twice. THREE MEASURED PLACEMENT AND SUPPORT FACTS, each a separate probe. (1) PLACEMENT IS AT THE CALLEE, NOT THE CALL SITE. `#pragma auto_inline off` bracketing the CALLER (LoadPlyrData) is a NO-OP: byte-identical result, real stayed 465, multiset stayed 43t. Auto-inline candidacy is decided where the callee is DEFINED, so bracket the callee's definition. This is the opposite placement from the dont_inline idiom this TU already uses around PlayerSfxClearData, which is why the earlier pass never found it. (2) THE COST ASYMMETRY VS dont_inline IS THE WHOLE POINT. Fact (3) of the dont-inline law measured that wrapping PlayerSfxInitData's definition in `dont_inline on/off` forced the calls but GREW THE CALLEE'S OWN FRAME 48 -> 56 (`stwu r1,-56` / `stmw r26,32`), demoting a byte-exact sibling to OPERAND_DIFF and making the form unusable under the never-regress-an-exact-function mandate. `auto_inline off` at the same site forced the same calls with the callee's frame and bytes UNCHANGED (defake_gate: 0 regressions, PlayerSfxInitData still real 0). The reason is that `dont_inline on` also blocks inlining INTO the bracketed region, changing the callee's own allocation; `auto_inline off` governs only whether the bracketed function may be inlined into OTHERS. When you need a `bl` and the callee is already exact, auto_inline is the correct tool and dont_inline is the wrong one. (3) THE `inline_max_*` PRAGMA FAMILY IS SILENTLY IGNORED by this compiler build and must not be spent probes on. Both `#pragma inline_max_auto_size(0)` and `#pragma inline_max_size(0)` compiled without any diagnostic and produced byte-identical output (real 465, multiset 43t, insns unchanged). `inline_max_size(0)` is the decisive control: had it been honoured it would have collapsed all 70 explicit swap-helper expansions into calls and exploded the diff; nothing moved, so the pragma never reached codegen. Unknown pragmas here are accepted silently, so a NEUTRAL probe on a pragma is evidence the pragma is UNSUPPORTED, not evidence the mechanism is unavailable. SCREENING ORDER for the 'target has a bl where we inline' residual: try `auto_inline off` around the callee definition FIRST (cheap, byte-neutral for the callee, compatible with explicit-inline helpers); reach for dont_inline only when the callee's own bytes are allowed to move; never spend a probe on inline_max_size / inline_max_auto_size.
